symptom: `dataview dv (…, OnClick: SHOW_PAGE …)` parses, `mxcli check` is clean, `exec` writes the page without a word — and the rendered element has no handler and no role="button". The same silence on `dynamictext`, `listview` and every other widget except a container or a button.
cause: `OnClick:` is an ALIAS for `Action:` (both stored as Properties["Action"], #603), and mxcli writes that property for three widget kinds only: container/customcontainer, the buttons, and a navigationlist item. Every other widget drops it, and the property allow-lists behind MDL-WIDGET01/07 could not see that because they are widget-type AGNOSTIC — the same blind spot as #928's `editable:`. Added MDL-WIDGET23 (warning), with two messages: Mendix models no click action at all (dataview, dynamictext, inputs, groupbox…) vs Mendix models one that mxcli cannot write (listview, staticimage, dynamicimage — measured against generated/metamodel).
insight: The first draft reported everything OUTSIDE an allow-list of the three writers, and running it over the shipped examples flagged three of them. Cause: `mxcli check` without `-p` has no widget registry, so `lookupWidgetDef` returns nil for a PLUGGABLE widget too and the caller's "static widgets only" branch silently does not hold — `datagrid` is DataGrid 2, a pluggable widget whose onClick the engine does write. For any rule keyed on widget type, an allow-list makes the unknown case an ERROR and a deny-list makes it silence; pick the deny-list, because a missed warning costs nothing and a false one tells an author their working page is broken. Running a new rule across mdl-examples/ before wiring it up is what caught it — the same exercise #893 describes. Reported as CapTrackV2 FINDINGS §21.
